items.subject: eng

skill.en: Responding to an apology or excuse
skill.th: การตอบรับคำขอโทษหรือข้ออ้าง

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
A: I'm afraid I can't make it to the study group tonight — my grandmother is visiting.
B: ______ We'll fill you in tomorrow.

explanation.en: 'No worries' is a friendly way to accept someone's excuse, and B then offers to update them. 'You're welcome' and 'Don't mention it' answer thanks, not an apology; 'It doesn't matter for me' is a common error (we say 'to me').
explanation.th: 'No worries' ใช้ตอบรับเมื่ออีกฝ่ายขอโทษหรือบอกว่ามาไม่ได้ แล้ว B ก็เสนอจะเล่าให้ฟังพรุ่งนี้ ส่วน 'You're welcome' และ 'Don't mention it' ใช้ตอบคำขอบคุณ ไม่ใช่ตอบคำขอโทษ และ 'It doesn't matter for me' ผิด (ต้องเป็น to me)

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบคำถาม Would you mind if …?

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
A: Would you mind if I opened the window? It's really stuffy in here.
B: ______ I was about to do it myself.

explanation.en: 'Would you mind …?' asks whether something bothers you, so agreeing means saying 'Not at all'. 'Yes, of course' would mean B objects, which clashes with 'I was about to do it myself'; 'No, please don't' contradicts itself.
explanation.th: 'Would you mind …?' ถามว่าเรารังเกียจหรือไม่ ถ้ายินยอมต้องตอบ 'Not at all, go ahead.' การตอบ 'Yes' แปลว่ารังเกียจ ซึ่งขัดกับประโยคต่อมาที่ว่า B กำลังจะเปิดเองอยู่แล้ว ส่วน 'No, please don't' ขัดกันในตัวเอง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การปลอบใจ ให้กำลังใจ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
A: How did your presentation go?
B: Honestly, I was so nervous that my mind went blank halfway through.
A: ______ Everyone forgets a line now and then.

explanation.en: A goes on to say that everyone forgets things, so A is comforting B: 'Don't be too hard on yourself.' 'You should have been more careful' blames B; 'Break a leg!' wishes someone luck before a performance; 'That's a piece of cake' means something is easy.
explanation.th: ประโยคต่อมาของ A บอกว่าใคร ๆ ก็ลืมได้ แสดงว่า A กำลังปลอบใจ จึงตอบ 'Don't be too hard on yourself.' (อย่าโทษตัวเองมากเกินไป) ส่วน 'You should have been more careful' เป็นการตำหนิ 'Break a leg!' ใช้อวยพรก่อนขึ้นแสดง และ 'That's a piece of cake' แปลว่าง่ายมาก

choices: You should have been more careful.
Don't be too hard on yourself.

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับคำแนะนำ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
A: I've been offered places at two schools and I can't decide between them.
B: Why don't you list the pros and cons of each?
A: ______ Putting it on paper might make things clearer.

explanation.en: A then says writing things down 'might make things clearer', so A accepts the suggestion: 'I suppose that's worth a try.' 'I couldn't agree with you less' rejects it; 'It's up to you' wrongly hands the decision to B; 'I've already decided' contradicts 'I can't decide'.
explanation.th: A พูดต่อว่าการเขียนลงกระดาษอาจช่วยให้ชัดเจนขึ้น แสดงว่ายอมรับคำแนะนำ จึงตอบ 'I suppose that's worth a try.' ส่วน 'I couldn't agree with you less' คือไม่เห็นด้วยเลย 'It's up to you' คือแล้วแต่คุณ ซึ่งผิดบริบท และ 'I've already decided' ขัดกับที่บอกว่ายังตัดสินใจไม่ได้

choices: I suppose that's worth a try.
I couldn't agree with you less.
You've got a point, but I've already decided.

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยา + กรรม + to-infinitive

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem: The new policy is designed to ______ students to read more widely by giving them points for every book they review.

explanation.en: 'Encourage someone to do something' fits the pattern and the meaning. 'Suggest' cannot be followed by 'someone to do' (a common error), 'insist' needs 'on', and 'prevent' means the opposite and takes 'from + -ing'.
explanation.th: ใช้ 'encourage + คน + to + V' (สนับสนุนให้ทำ) ได้ทั้งรูปและความหมาย ส่วน suggest ใช้รูป suggest someone to do ไม่ได้ insist ต้องตามด้วย on และ prevent มีความหมายตรงข้ามและใช้ prevent … from + V-ing

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วม carry out

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem: Researchers have ______ a series of experiments to find out whether the new drug is safe for children.

explanation.en: We 'carry out' experiments, research or surveys. 'Make up' means invent, 'take over' means take control, and 'put off' means postpone.
explanation.th: 'carry out an experiment' แปลว่าดำเนินการทดลอง ส่วน make up แปลว่าแต่งขึ้น take over แปลว่าเข้าควบคุม และ put off แปลว่าเลื่อนออกไป

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเลือกคำคุณศัพท์ให้ถูกรูป

topic.th: การสร้างคำ

items.stem: The museum's decision to charge an entrance fee proved highly ______, and visitor numbers fell by half within a year.

explanation.en: After 'proved highly' we need an adjective: 'controversial'. 'Controversy' is a noun, 'controversially' an adverb and 'controvert' a verb.
explanation.th: หลัง proved highly ต้องใช้คำคุณศัพท์ คือ controversial (เป็นที่ถกเถียง) ส่วน controversy เป็นคำนาม controversially เป็นคำกริยาวิเศษณ์ และ controvert เป็นคำกริยา

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Meaning of an adjective in context
skill.th: ความหมายของคำคุณศัพท์ตามบริบท

topic.th: คำศัพท์เชิงวิชาการ

items.stem:
Despite the team's meticulous preparation, the experiment failed because of a faulty sensor.
The word 'meticulous' is closest in meaning to ______.

explanation.en: 'Despite' signals a contrast: the preparation was good, yet the experiment failed. 'Meticulous' means very careful, paying attention to every detail.
explanation.th: 'Despite' บอกความขัดแย้ง คือเตรียมการดีแต่ก็ยังล้มเหลว meticulous แปลว่าละเอียดรอบคอบมาก (very careful and thorough)

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยาวลีกับ give

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem: Many villagers had to ______ fishing when the river became polluted, and most of them turned to farming instead.

explanation.en: 'Give up' means stop doing something, which matches 'turned to farming instead'. 'Give in' means surrender, 'give off' means produce a smell or heat, and 'give away' means give something for free.
explanation.th: give up แปลว่าเลิกทำ เข้ากับที่ว่าหันไปทำนาแทน ส่วน give in แปลว่ายอมแพ้ give off แปลว่าปล่อยกลิ่นหรือความร้อนออกมา และ give away แปลว่าแจกให้ฟรี

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วม narrow the gap

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem: The government has promised to ______ the gap between rich and poor regions by investing in rural schools.

explanation.en: The fixed collocation is 'narrow (or close) the gap'. 'Shorten' is used for length or time, 'tighten' for screws or rules, and 'lessen down' is not English.
explanation.th: สำนวนที่ใช้คือ narrow the gap (ลดช่องว่าง) ส่วน shorten ใช้กับความยาวหรือเวลา tighten ใช้กับการขันให้แน่นหรือกฎที่เข้มงวดขึ้น และ lessen down ไม่มีใช้ในภาษาอังกฤษ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำคุณศัพท์เชิงวิชาการจากบริบท

topic.th: คำศัพท์เชิงวิชาการ

items.stem: The results were ______: some participants improved dramatically, while others showed no change at all.

explanation.en: The colon introduces evidence that the results varied widely, so 'inconsistent' (not the same throughout) fits. 'Unanimous' means everyone agreed, 'inevitable' means certain to happen, and 'insignificant' means too small to matter — but some changes were dramatic.
explanation.th: เครื่องหมาย : ตามด้วยหลักฐานว่าผลแตกต่างกันมาก จึงใช้ inconsistent (ไม่สม่ำเสมอ) ส่วน unanimous แปลว่าเป็นเอกฉันท์ inevitable แปลว่าหลีกเลี่ยงไม่ได้ insignificant แปลว่าไม่สำคัญ ซึ่งขัดกับที่บางคนพัฒนาขึ้นอย่างมาก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำคุณศัพท์ที่สับสนง่าย

topic.th: คำศัพท์เชิงวิชาการ

items.stem: Her argument was so ______ that even the students who had disagreed with her at first were won over.

explanation.en: A 'compelling' argument is convincing, which explains why opponents were 'won over'. 'Compulsory' means required by a rule, 'complacent' means too satisfied with oneself, and 'compatible' means able to work together.
explanation.th: compelling แปลว่าน่าเชื่อถือ โน้มน้าวใจได้ จึงทำให้คนที่ไม่เห็นด้วยเปลี่ยนใจ ส่วน compulsory แปลว่าบังคับ complacent แปลว่าพอใจในตัวเองจนประมาท และ compatible แปลว่าเข้ากันได้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Past perfect for an earlier past action
skill.th: past perfect กับเหตุการณ์ที่เกิดก่อนในอดีต

topic.th: กาล (Tense)

items.stem: By the time the ambulance arrived, the injured man ______ consciousness.

explanation.en: 'By the time + past simple' shows that the other action was completed earlier, so the past perfect 'had already lost' is needed.
explanation.th: 'By the time + past simple' บอกว่าอีกเหตุการณ์หนึ่งเสร็จไปก่อนแล้ว จึงใช้ past perfect คือ had already lost

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Second conditional: if I were you
skill.th: เงื่อนไขแบบที่ 2: If I were you

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem: If I ______ you, I would apologise to her before the rumour spreads any further.

explanation.en: Advice with 'I would …' uses the second conditional: 'If I were you'. 'Had been' belongs to the third conditional (with 'would have'), and 'am' or 'will be' do not match 'would'.
explanation.th: การให้คำแนะนำด้วย I would … ใช้เงื่อนไขแบบที่ 2 คือ If I were you ส่วน had been ใช้กับเงื่อนไขแบบที่ 3 (คู่กับ would have) และ am / will be ไม่เข้ากับ would

items.subject: eng

skill.th: อนุประโยคขยายแบบไม่จำกัดความ

topic.th: อนุประโยคและคำเชื่อม

items.stem: The bridge, ______ was completed in 1932, is still used by thousands of commuters every day.

explanation.en: The commas show a non-defining relative clause, which takes 'which' (not 'that') for things. 'What' cannot refer back to a noun, and 'it' would create two clauses with no connector.
explanation.th: มีเครื่องหมายจุลภาคล้อมรอบ จึงเป็น non-defining relative clause ต้องใช้ which ไม่ใช้ that ส่วน what ใช้แทนคำนามข้างหน้าไม่ได้ และ it จะทำให้มีสองประโยคโดยไม่มีคำเชื่อม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: suggest + V-ing

topic.th: รูปแบบกริยา (gerund/infinitive)

items.stem: At the meeting, the head teacher suggested ______ the trip until everyone had read the safety report.

explanation.en: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund (or a that-clause), not by 'to + verb' or 'someone to + verb'. So 'suggested postponing' is correct.
explanation.th: suggest ตามด้วย V-ing (หรือ that-clause) ไม่ใช้ to + V หรือ คน + to + V จึงต้องเป็น suggested postponing

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเรียงคำในคำถามแบบรายงาน

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องและการเรียงคำ

items.stem: He asked me where ______ the previous weekend.

explanation.en: In reported questions the word order is like a statement (subject + verb), and the tense moves back: 'where I had been'. 'Had I been' and 'did I go' keep question order.
explanation.th: คำถามในประโยครายงานต้องเรียงแบบประโยคบอกเล่า (ประธาน + กริยา) และเลื่อน tense ถอยหลัง จึงเป็น where I had been ส่วน had I been และ did I go ยังเรียงแบบคำถาม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: Despite กับ although

topic.th: อนุประโยคและคำเชื่อม

items.stem: ______ the heavy traffic, we reached the airport in time for our flight.

explanation.en: A noun phrase ('the heavy traffic') follows, so we need a preposition: 'Despite'. 'Although' needs a clause, 'In spite' needs 'of', and 'However' is an adverb that cannot join a noun to a clause.
explanation.th: ตามด้วยนามวลี the heavy traffic จึงต้องใช้บุพบท Despite ส่วน Although ต้องตามด้วยประโยค In spite ต้องมี of และ However เป็นคำกริยาวิเศษณ์ที่เชื่อมนามวลีกับประโยคไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: passive กับ modal verb

topic.th: ประโยค passive

items.stem: All mobile phones must ______ at the front desk before candidates enter the examination room.

explanation.en: Phones do not leave themselves; they are left by candidates, so the passive 'must be left' is needed.
explanation.th: โทรศัพท์ไม่ได้ทำกริยาเอง แต่ถูกผู้สอบนำมาฝากไว้ จึงต้องใช้ passive คือ must be left

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสลับที่หลัง Not until

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องและการเรียงคำ

items.stem: Not until the last guest had left ______ how exhausted she was.

explanation.en: When a sentence begins with 'Not until …', the main clause uses question-style inversion: 'did she realise'.
explanation.th: เมื่อขึ้นต้นประโยคด้วย Not until … ประโยคหลักต้องสลับที่แบบคำถาม จึงเป็น did she realise

items.subject: eng

skill.th: future perfect แบบ passive

topic.th: ประโยค passive

items.stem: The new library ______ by the end of next year, so students will have to study elsewhere until then.

explanation.en: 'By the end of next year' points to an action finished before a future time (future perfect), and the library is completed by someone else (passive): 'will have been completed'.
explanation.th: 'By the end of next year' บอกว่าจะเสร็จก่อนเวลาหนึ่งในอนาคต (future perfect) และห้องสมุดถูกสร้างโดยผู้อื่น (passive) จึงเป็น will have been completed

items.subject: eng

skill.th: would rather + past simple

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem: I'd rather you ______ my phone without asking me first.

explanation.en: When 'would rather' is followed by a different subject, the verb goes into the past simple to talk about the present or future: 'I'd rather you didn't use …'.
explanation.th: เมื่อ would rather ตามด้วยประธานคนละคน กริยาต้องเป็น past simple แม้จะพูดถึงปัจจุบันหรืออนาคต จึงเป็น I'd rather you didn't use …

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ความสอดคล้องของประธานกับกริยา: every one of

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องและการเรียงคำ

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: Every one of the students [[who]] [[took]] the test [[were]] given a certificate [[at]] the end of the course.

explanation.en: The subject is 'every one', which is singular, so the verb must be 'was given', not 'were given'.
explanation.th: ประธานคือ every one ซึ่งเป็นเอกพจน์ กริยาจึงต้องเป็น was given ไม่ใช่ were given

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ใช้คำเชื่อมซ้อน although … but

topic.th: อนุประโยคและคำเชื่อม

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: [[Although]] it was raining heavily, [[but]] the match [[went ahead]] [[as planned]].

explanation.en: 'Although' already links the two clauses, so 'but' must be removed. English does not use 'although … but' together, a common error for Thai speakers (แม้ว่า … แต่).
explanation.th: Although เชื่อมสองประโยคอยู่แล้ว จึงต้องตัด but ออก ภาษาอังกฤษไม่ใช้ although คู่กับ but แบบภาษาไทย 'แม้ว่า … แต่'

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ความสอดคล้องกับ the number of

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องและการเรียงคำ

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: The number of tourists [[visiting]] the island [[have risen]] sharply [[since]] the new airport [[opened]].

explanation.en: 'The number of …' is singular, so the verb should be 'has risen'. (Compare 'A number of tourists have …', which is plural.)
explanation.th: 'The number of …' เป็นเอกพจน์ กริยาจึงต้องเป็น has risen (ต่างจาก A number of … ที่เป็นพหูพจน์)

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้เวลาในประโยคเงื่อนไข

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: She [[failed]] the exam in March; if she [[had studied]] harder, she [[would pass]] it [[easily]].

explanation.en: The whole sentence is about the past (she failed in March), so it is a third conditional: 'she would have passed it'.
explanation.th: ทั้งประโยคพูดถึงอดีต (สอบตกเมื่อเดือนมีนาคม) จึงเป็นเงื่อนไขแบบที่ 3 ต้องใช้ would have passed

items.subject: eng

skill.th: spend time + V-ing

topic.th: รูปแบบกริยา (gerund/infinitive)

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: The report, [[which]] was published last week, [[suggests]] that teenagers [[should]] spend less time [[to look]] at screens.

explanation.en: 'Spend time' is followed by the -ing form: 'spend less time looking at screens'.
explanation.th: spend time ต้องตามด้วย V-ing จึงต้องเป็น spend less time looking at screens

items.subject: eng

skill.th: participle ที่ประธานไม่ตรงกัน (dangling participle)

topic.th: อนุประโยคและคำเชื่อม

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: [[Having finished]] the essay, the computer [[suddenly]] crashed and she [[lost]] [[everything]].

explanation.en: A participle clause takes the subject of the main clause, so this says the computer finished the essay. It should be 'After she had finished the essay, the computer …'.
explanation.th: วลี participle ต้องมีประธานเดียวกับประโยคหลัก ประโยคนี้จึงแปลว่าคอมพิวเตอร์เขียนเรียงความเสร็จ ต้องแก้เป็น After she had finished the essay, the computer …

items.subject: eng

skill.th: look forward to + V-ing

items.passage:
In a mountain on a remote Arctic island, a tunnel leads to a set of frozen chambers holding more than a million packets of seeds. The facility is often called a 'doomsday vault', but the people who run it dislike the name. Its purpose, they say, is not to prepare for the end of the world but to protect against the far more ordinary losses that happen every year.

Around the world there are more than 1,700 seed banks, most of them national or regional. They store samples of crops such as rice, wheat and maize, along with their wild relatives. These collections matter because modern agriculture depends on a surprisingly small number of varieties. If a new disease attacks one of them, plant breeders need to find genes for resistance, and the most likely place to find them is in older or wild types of the same plant. A seed bank is, in effect, a library of genetic possibilities.

Yet many of these libraries are fragile. Some have lost their collections to floods, power cuts or simple lack of funding; others have been damaged by war. In 2015, researchers in the Middle East became the first to withdraw seeds from the Arctic vault after fighting forced them to abandon their own gene bank. Using the copies they had deposited years earlier, they were able to rebuild much of their collection in new locations.

Storing seeds is not as simple as putting them in a freezer. Each sample must be dried carefully, sealed in foil packets and kept at around minus eighteen degrees Celsius. Even then, seeds do not last for ever. Their ability to germinate declines over time, so staff must regularly test samples and grow fresh plants to produce new seed. For some species, such as coconuts and many tropical fruits, freezing does not work at all, because their seeds die when they are dried. These must be conserved as living plants in fields or as tissue samples in laboratories.

Critics argue that seed banks can create a false sense of security. A frozen seed, they point out, is cut off from the changing climate and the evolving pests that a plant in a farmer's field must adapt to. For this reason, many scientists believe that vaults should complement, not replace, the work of farmers who continue to grow traditional varieties.
items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

explanation.en: The text explains why seed banks matter (genetic resources, rebuilding lost collections) and then their limits (storage problems, seeds that cannot be frozen, a false sense of security). The vault and the war are only examples.

items.passage:
In a mountain on a remote Arctic island, a tunnel leads to a set of frozen chambers holding more than a million packets of seeds. The facility is often called a 'doomsday vault', but the people who run it dislike the name. Its purpose, they say, is not to prepare for the end of the world but to protect against the far more ordinary losses that happen every year.

Around the world there are more than 1,700 seed banks, most of them national or regional. They store samples of crops such as rice, wheat and maize, along with their wild relatives. These collections matter because modern agriculture depends on a surprisingly small number of varieties. If a new disease attacks one of them, plant breeders need to find genes for resistance, and the most likely place to find them is in older or wild types of the same plant. A seed bank is, in effect, a library of genetic possibilities.

Yet many of these libraries are fragile. Some have lost their collections to floods, power cuts or simple lack of funding; others have been damaged by war. In 2015, researchers in the Middle East became the first to withdraw seeds from the Arctic vault after fighting forced them to abandon their own gene bank. Using the copies they had deposited years earlier, they were able to rebuild much of their collection in new locations.

Storing seeds is not as simple as putting them in a freezer. Each sample must be dried carefully, sealed in foil packets and kept at around minus eighteen degrees Celsius. Even then, seeds do not last for ever. Their ability to germinate declines over time, so staff must regularly test samples and grow fresh plants to produce new seed. For some species, such as coconuts and many tropical fruits, freezing does not work at all, because their seeds die when they are dried. These must be conserved as living plants in fields or as tissue samples in laboratories.

Critics argue that seed banks can create a false sense of security. A frozen seed, they point out, is cut off from the changing climate and the evolving pests that a plant in a farmer's field must adapt to. For this reason, many scientists believe that vaults should complement, not replace, the work of farmers who continue to grow traditional varieties.

Ploy had never intended to enter the debate competition. Her English teacher, Mr Anan, had simply written her name on the list and told her afterwards, as if he were doing her a favour. 'You argue with me in every lesson,' he said. 'You might as well get a certificate for it.'

The motion was announced two weeks before the contest: 'Homework should be abolished.' Ploy's team was told to oppose it, which struck her as deeply unfair. She had complained about homework for most of her life, and now she was expected to defend it in front of an audience of strangers.

For the first few days she barely prepared. She told herself that the other team had the easier side and that losing would not be her fault. Then, one evening, she found her younger brother in tears over a page of fractions. She sat down to help him, intending to give him the answers so that they could both go to bed. Instead, she found herself asking him questions, and gradually he worked out the method himself. When he finished, he looked more pleased than she had seen him in weeks.

Ploy went to her room and opened her notebook. She did not write that homework was enjoyable, because she did not believe it. What she wrote was that practice done alone, without a teacher nearby, showed students what they actually understood rather than what they thought they understood. She added that the real problem was not homework itself but homework that was set without thought: pages of repetition that taught nothing new.

On the day of the competition her hands were shaking so badly that she left her notes on the table and spoke without them. She told the story of her brother and the fractions. She admitted that she had thought she was on the wrong side at first, and the audience laughed. Then she argued that abolishing homework would punish students like her brother, who needed quiet practice to build confidence, while doing nothing about the real issue — the quality of the tasks.

Her team did not win. The judges praised their honesty but felt that the other side had used more evidence. On the bus home, Mr Anan asked if she was disappointed. Ploy thought for a moment. 'A little,' she said. 'But I think I changed my own mind, and that's harder than changing anyone else's.'

Her brother persuaded her to enter.

Every few months another country or school district announces that it will ban mobile phones from classrooms, and the news is usually greeted with relief. Teachers are tired of competing with screens; parents worry about cyberbullying and sleepless nights. On the surface, a ban seems like the obvious answer. I want to argue, however, that a complete ban is the wrong tool for a real problem.

Let me begin with what the supporters of bans get right. There is solid evidence that the mere presence of a phone on a desk reduces concentration, even when it is switched off. Students who are allowed to check messages during lessons tend to remember less, and the constant comparison encouraged by social media can damage self-esteem. Nobody seriously disputes that unrestricted phone use in school is harmful.

The difficulty lies in assuming that removing the device removes the problem. Most teenagers will spend several hours a day on their phones whatever the school rules say; the habits that matter are formed at home, on the bus and late at night. A school that simply locks phones away from eight until four teaches students nothing about how to manage them for the other sixteen hours. It is a little like trying to teach road safety by keeping children indoors.

There is also a question of fairness. For many families, particularly those who cannot afford a laptop, a phone is the only device a student owns. It is their dictionary, their calculator and their way of contacting a parent who works long shifts. A blanket ban treats a tool for learning and a source of distraction as though they were the same thing.

What I propose instead is a policy of deliberate use. Phones should be out of sight by default, stored in bags or lockers, but teachers should be free to ask students to take them out for specific tasks: recording an experiment, checking a source, practising pronunciation. Alongside this, schools should teach digital habits as seriously as any other subject — how notifications are designed to capture attention, how to turn them off, how to recognise when scrolling has replaced rest.

Bans are attractive because they are simple to announce and easy to measure. Teaching self-control is slower and harder to show in a report. But the aim of education is not to produce students who behave well only when temptation is removed. It is to prepare them for a world in which it never will be.
items.stem: What is the writer's main argument?

explanation.en: The writer calls a complete ban 'the wrong tool' and proposes 'deliberate use' plus teaching digital habits. Free use in lessons is rejected too ('unrestricted phone use … is harmful').

choices: Parents, not schools, are responsible for teenagers' phone habits.
Students should be allowed to use phones freely during lessons.
Schools should teach students to manage phones rather than banning them completely.
Phones should be banned because they damage concentration.

It is a little like trying to teach road safety by keeping children indoors.
